comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `getFinishTimeLabel()` computes `finishDate` from `Date.now() + minutes * 60000`, but the `minutes` value passed in is the *rounded* `totalRemainingMinutes` (Math.ceil of remaining time). Because the component re-renders every second while the timer runs, the displayed/announced finish time can drift later while `totalRemainingMinutes` stays constant, and can be off by up to ~1 minute due to the ceil. Consider basing the finish timestamp on the unrounded remaining duration (e.g., use a `rawRemainingMinutes` float before the `Math.ceil`, or compute remaining seconds/ms directly) so the estimated completion time is stable/monotonic and matches the remaining-time math used elsewhere.

comments.author: google-labs-jules
comments.body: Acknowledged. I've refactored the finish time calculation to be more deterministic. By using fractional remaining minutes and stabilizing the calculation within a `useMemo` block, the estimated finish time now remains constant as the timer progresses, only updating if the task estimates themselves are modified. This eliminates visual jitter while providing accurate temporal grounding.
